MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  April 11, 2017

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Bucknum at 5:00 p.m., on April 11, 2017, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on April 6, 2017, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Raths
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
  Mayor Bucknum (departed at 5:48 p.m.)

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957 and 54957.6. The Parties to the
  Negotiations Are the City and City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s
  Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.

CS2. Conference with Real Property Negotiators. Property: APN 808-720-07, APN 808-
  571-01, APN 808-720-08, APN 808-720-09, APN 808-720-10, APN 808-720-11, APN
City Council Minutes  1  April 11, 2017
   808-720-12, APN 808-132-16. Agency Negotiators: City Manager Wilberg; Assistant
  City Manager Rattay; Community Development Director Lister; Administrative
  Services Director Dyas, City Attorney. Negotiating Parties: NGP Realty. Under
  Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with four City Council Members present. Mayor Bucknum had
a work commitment and departed the meeting after the Closed Session at 5:48 p.m.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council considered three Closed Session
items. They received information and gave direction to staff but there was no reportable action on
any of the Closed Session matters.

INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Raths

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Presentation by the Child Abuse Prevention Center

  The City Council received the presentation from Child Abuse Prevention Center Executive
  Director, Scott Trotter.

P2.  Proclaim April 9 through April 15, 2017 to Be National Library Week

  Director of Library and Cultural Services Genesis Hansen discussed National Library
  Week and Mayor Pro Tem Sachs presented the City's proclamation.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

J. Alan Schumann, Ph.D: thanked the City for approving the Trabuco Hills High School
community outreach program to educate youth about making mature decisions when alcoholic
beverages are involved. The two-day program is for junior and senior students and he invited the
Council Members to witness a mock DUI crash on Tuesday, May 23 at THHS. The program,
known as "Every 15 Minutes," will continue on May 24 with an assembly in the school’s
gymnasium.

Victor Gonzalez, M.V.: stated that it is not proper for the people of Mission Viejo to try and compel
the Council Members to produce or influence a response from other elected government officials,
especially those that are in a higher office.
City Council Minutes  2  April 11, 2017
 Deborah Cunningham-Skurnik, M.V.: discussed H.R.610, a bill that will repeal the Elementary
and Secondary Education Act of 1965 and will change American public schools by establishing a
voucher system. She said it would be in the City's best interest to encourage Congresswoman Mimi
Walters to vote no on the bill and to hold a town hall meeting in Mission Viejo.

Ayesha Medue, M.V.: stated that she is a new resident of Mission Viejo and has recently become
a naturalized citizen of the United States. She asked for Mayor Bucknum's influence in getting
Congresswoman Mimi Walters to hold a Town Hall meeting for Mission Viejo residents.

Annie Nelson, founder of the American Soldier Network, M.V.: read a letter that she received
from Congresswoman Mimi Walters which confirms that Mayor Wendy Bucknum attended a
February 22 meeting with the Congresswoman as a guest of Ms. Nelson's and not as a
representative of the City.

Raydene South, M.V.: stated that her comments were inaccurately summarized in the Minutes of
the March 28, 2017, City Council Meeting for the Vision Plan (agenda item 9) and she asked how
the Minutes might be corrected.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: said that the Mission Viejo Garden Plaza is for sale and she voiced concern
that there is an opportunity for housing at the location. She also expressed dissatisfaction with the
summary of speakers in the March 28 Minutes and said that they have been stacked by city hall to
establish a predetermined outcome.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Item 2 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Raths, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Bucknum

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

3.  Check Register Dated March 17, 2017 in the Amount of $692,630.17

City Council Minutes  3  April 11, 2017
   Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated March 24, 2017 in the Amount of $928,116.55

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for February 2017

  Received and filed.

6.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for February 2017

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for February
  2017

  Received and filed.

8.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for February 2017

  Received and filed.

9.  Marguerite Parkway Median Island Improvements: Alarcon to Santa Margarita
  Parkway (CIP 229)

  Approved the plans and specifications and authorized staff to advertise for bids for the
  Marguerite Parkway Median Island Improvements, Alarcon to Santa Margarita Parkway
  (CIP 229).

10.  Marguerite Parkway Corridor Traffic Signal Synchronization Project (CIP 230)

  (1) Authorized issuance of a purchase order to Iteris, Inc., in an amount not to exceed
  $259,050 for design engineering services for the subject project; and (2) adopted
  Resolution 17-13 Amending the Fiscal Year 2016?2017 Budget for Costs Related to
  Capital Improvement Project 230.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Sheila Edmond, M.V.: stated that her comments at the last meeting were lumped into a
  general category of support for the Vision Plan. While she did say she is in favor of some
City Council Minutes  4  April 11, 2017
   beautification and modernization, she said she gave some qualifications and therefore
  asked that the Minutes be corrected.

  Raydene South, M.V.: said that she is actually not in favor of the civic core project but she
  was lumped into the "in favor" group in the March 28 Minutes. Ms. South stated that she
  is opposed to vertical buildings, housing, parking structures, and increased traffic in the
  area.

  City Clerk Karen Hamman noted that she will listen to the video tape from the last Council
  Meeting and will amend the Minutes where necessary. The updated Minutes will be
  brought to the City Council at the next meeting.

  By consensus, the City Council tabled the item to April 25, 2017.

OLD BUSINESS

11.  Annual Routine Maintenance Schedule and City Council Consideration of Contract
  Renewals

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Pat Mahoney, President of West Coast Arborists: discussed West Coast Arborists (WAC)
  service to Mission Viejo for the past 24 years. He outlined issues surrounding the
  new California prevailing wages for tree maintenance laborers which has caused WAC to
  request a price adjustment of 30% effective July 1, 2017. The increase would be
  implemented at 10% per year for three years.

  Jeff Melin, Great Scott Tree Service, Rancho Santa Margarita: offered ideas regarding the
  tree maintenance contract and recommended that the City go out to bid instead of renewing
  the current contract.

  The following presented a written letter requesting that the City issue a formal bid for tree
  maintenance services: Scott P. Griffiths, President, Great Scott Tree Service.

  Motion made by Council Member Raths, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to return
  to the City Council with contract renewals as outlined in the staff report.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

City Council Minutes  5  April 11, 2017
 MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

12.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs announced that he was out of town last week and did not attend the
  OCFA Board meeting.

STAFF REPORTS

13.  Orange County Sheriff’s Department (OCSD) Update

  Lieutenant Binning announced that there are three new deputies assigned to the City and
  all OCSD deputies have now been trained to administer a medication that rapidly reverses
  opioid overdose. Since the program was instituted in October 2016, there have been 17
  lives saved countywide, with two of those in Mission Viejo. Lieutenant Binning announced
  that last week’s Tip-a-Cop fundraiser generated $2,300 for Special Olympics and
  tomorrow there will be a Coffee with a Cop event at Starbucks on La Paz Road from 8:00
  a.m. to 10:00 a.m.

City Manager Report

City Manager Wilberg announced that he distributed the monthly update on the progress at the
Marguerite Aquatics Complex and Assistant City Manager Rattay noted that the work is going
well, now that the rain has stopped.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

14.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Goodell

Thanked Lieutenant Binning for the very good report and he said he was moved to know that there
were 17 lives saved by the Orange County Sheriff’s Department via an opioid overdose reversal
medication. He thanked Lt. Binning and the Mission Viejo deputies for their great work. Council
Member Goodell said that he attended the memorial service for Ziggy Wilczynski and he thanked
staff for doing a great job in memorializing “Mr. Mission Viejo.”

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley reminded residents of upcoming events including Bunny Days on
Saturday, April 15 at Oso Viejo Park; Earth Day/Arbor Day on Saturday April 22 from 8 a.m. to
City Council Minutes  6  April 11, 2017
 12:00 p.m. on Mustang Run at Los Alisos Boulevard; and Arts Alive on April 29 and 30 at Oso
Viejo Community Park on the Village Green. Council Member Kelley noted that she has been
attending Character Committee meetings and the group is predominately made up of high school
students with a few adults. The committee plans meaningful activities that promote good character
in the community. At its next meeting on April 19, the committee will be hearing a presentation
from Jodi Barber regarding the prescription drug abuse epidemic and will look at the movies
Overtaken and Behind the Orange Curtain to consider whether the committee can help promote
the films. Council Member Kelley announced that the Community of Character word for the month
of April is service and she thanked Chamber of Commerce member Bob Morris with Documedia
for donating the two-page character fliers for every teacher in every Mission Viejo school. She
stated that the character program is making a difference in the City.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths announced that he attended the Saddleback College Foundation gala last
weekend and he joked that he inadvertently bought an item in the auction. He also discussed a
conversation he had with the Orange County Tax Collector, Claude Parrish, a couple of years ago
and, as a result, Mission Viejo now hosts a satellite County Assessor’s office on the 2nd floor of
city hall. There will be a grand opening event on May 23 from 3:00 to 5:00 p.m. and he said it is
nice that residents will no longer have to drive all the way to Santa Ana for those services. Council
Member Raths noted that most speeding tickets in Mission Viejo are given on Oso Parkway and
he has written an article for the Mission Viejo Reporter newspaper encouraging residents to slow
down when driving in town. He also discussed a letter he received from a resident thanking him
for his help in getting “ALL-Way” plaque signs installed underneath each of the four stop signs at
Peter Hartman Way and Via Fabricante. In closing, Council Member Raths thanked the Sherriff’s
deputies for doing a great job to keep the City safe.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs noted that while reviewing the agenda for tonight’s meeting, he was
reminded that not all contracts are paid for from the general fund and he asked staff to provide a
contract list showing where the money comes from. He announced that he will be attending a
disaster drill at the Orange County Airport with the Orange County Fire Authority later this week
and he said that he looks forward to learning more about what the firefighters do for the public’s
benefit. Mayor Pro Tem Sachs thanked residents for coming to the City Council meetings and
especially those who stay to listen so they better understand what the Council Members can and
cannot do.

Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum was absent.

City Council Minutes  7  April 11, 2017
 ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:21 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Pro Tem Sachs adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, April 25, 2017, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of April 25, 2017

City Council Minutes  8  April 11, 2017
